title: What is session feedback and how does it work?
seoTitle: Session Feedback in augo: How It Works | augo support
description: Session feedback is the short set of questions augo asks an athlete after every workout. Coaches choose which questions appear; three are always asked.
summary: After each workout, augo asks the athlete a short set of questions about how the session actually felt — energy, effort, fuelling, aches and anything else worth flagging. Coaches pick which of the 11 available questions their athletes see, and three of them are always asked.

body.html:
Workout files tell you what an athlete did. They don't tell you what it cost them. Session feedback is how augo captures the second half of that picture — a short, structured check-in attached to each session, so the athlete's own account of the workout sits next to the data from their watch.

Because the answers are structured rather than free-form chat, augo can track them over time and surface changes as trends, instead of leaving them buried in a message thread.

What athletes are asked

There are 11 questions in the library, grouped into four areas. Coaches choose which optional ones to switch on — see choosing which feedback questions your athletes see.

How they felt

  • Energy level before training — low energy, normal, or high energy.
  • How did you feel during training? — struggled/bad, average/normal, or strong/great. Always asked.
  • How hard did it feel? (RPE) — a five-point scale described in plain language, from "Very easy — like a relaxing walk" through to "Maximum effort — all-out, couldn't go harder".

Fuel & hydration

  • What did you consume before the session?
  • Carbs consumed per hour
  • What did you consume during the session?
  • Did you have any digestive or gut issues? — had issues, felt OK, or dialled in.

Recovery & other

  • How did you recover between intervals/sets? — recovered quickly, took some time, or struggled to recover.
  • Any aches or pains? — no issues, minor discomfort, or something concerning. Always asked.
  • How do you feel about your performance during this session? — below, met, or exceeded expectations.

Notes

  • Anything else to add? — free text. Always asked.

The three questions that are always asked

Three questions are required and can't be switched off:

  1. How did you feel during training?
  2. Any aches or pains?
  3. Anything else to add?

They're fixed because they're the ones that catch problems early. "Something concerning" on the aches question is the single most useful signal augo collects — it's the difference between hearing about an injury now and hearing about it in three weeks.

Everything else is the coach's call. A time-crunched age-grouper and an athlete deep in a fuelling block don't need the same questionnaire.

Writing or speaking the answer

The free-text questions accept typing or a voice note. Voice notes are transcribed automatically, so a rushed two-sentence recording after a long ride still ends up searchable and readable alongside everything else.

In practice this is what gets feedback completion rates up. Athletes who won't type a paragraph on a phone will happily talk for twenty seconds.

What happens to the answers

Answers are visible to the athlete's coach against the session they belong to, and they feed two things:

  • Trends. Both coach and athlete can see how the answers move over weeks and months, which is where fatigue, motivation dips and niggles-becoming-injuries become visible.
  • The daily priority list. augo weighs feedback alongside workout data when deciding which athletes to surface for attention. See what the daily priority list is.

Feedback is part of the coaching record between an athlete and their coach. It isn't shared with other athletes, and it isn't used to train models served to athletes.

faqs.question: How many session feedback questions are there?
faqs.answer: There are 11 questions available, across four groups: how they felt, fuel and hydration, recovery and other, and notes. Coaches choose which optional questions their athletes see, and three questions are always asked.

faqs.question: Which session feedback questions can't be turned off?
faqs.answer: Three are required: "How did you feel during training?", "Any aches or pains?", and "Anything else to add?". They're fixed because they're the questions most likely to catch a developing problem early.

faqs.question: Can athletes answer session feedback by voice?
faqs.answer: Yes. Free-text questions accept a typed answer or a voice note, and voice notes are transcribed automatically so they're searchable alongside everything else.

faqs.question: Does the athlete see their own feedback trends?
faqs.answer: Yes. Feedback isn't only logged for the coach — trends are visible to both the athlete and their coach, so early warning signs can be spotted together.
